title: Unix address namespaces are pathname, abstract, or unnamed
summary: UnixAddress models three distinct address forms instead of flattening every endpoint into a pathname string: filesystem pathname, Linux abstract namespace, and genuinely unnamed addresses.
invariants: PATHNAME addresses reject embedded NUL bytes and include a terminating NUL in sockaddr_un.
ABSTRACT addresses are binary-safe and may contain embedded NUL bytes; the kernel namespace begins with an initial NUL byte.
UNNAMED is a real address state, including unbound datagram peers; it is not an empty pathname.
Address-length limits come from the qualified ABI profile rather than a magic number in application code.
procedure: Use UnixAddress~pathname, ~abstract, or ~unnamed according to the kernel namespace being represented.

provenance.claim: UnixAddress source implements PATHNAME, ABSTRACT and UNNAMED namespaces with NUL and length rules and binary-safe native encoding/decoding.
